idle: Did you know Moose Kowalczuk has 3,644 penalty minutes? That's like two days in the box.
I've got a double Milkman card. Doubles are for trading.
My dad is somewhere. Please don't tell him I'm here.
good_ice: The ice is fast today. I'm fast today.
Good ice. Even my dad could skate on this.
bad_ice: There's a rut by the blue line. I fell in it. Twice. Not on purpose.
wet_ice: It's soggy. My socks are soggy. Everything's soggy.
goal: Okay that was a good one.
cold: My fingers are numb. That's how you know you're tough.
I can't feel my feet. Normal.
hungry: Can I get a Haverstock? It's got fourteen marshmallows. I counted once.
long_line: This line is longer than my dad's stories.
bored: Want to hear a fact? Okay. I'll tell you anyway.
greet_owner: Hi {owner}. Want to trade a fact?
Hey. My dad's not here. I checked.
leaving_happy: I did a backwards crossover. Dad still can't.
leaving_angry: That was the worst. Saturday practice is too early anyway.

minor_hockey: I'm on the second line. It's basically the first line.
Coach says pass more. I pass sometimes.
tournament: Tommy says Kessler pins are worth three of ours. Is that true?
Tournament day! I've been dressed since six.
pro_practice: The Dukes! I'm getting a stick. Tommy says I won't. I will.

first.say: Hi. I'm Owen. Pruett. P-R-U-E-T-T. Not Pruitt. Not Maddie's brother. Not Gary's kid. Well, I am Gary's kid, but don't say it.

options.text: Your dad's the one who stops in front of the bench?

first_dad.say: Every single time. He makes a little 'whoosh' noise with his mouth when he does it. It's so embarrassing.

options.text: I'll pretend I've never seen it.
Saturday practice at seven again? I'll talk to the schedule.

say: I'm dressed. I've been dressed for an hour. Is it time yet?
My dad's at the glass. He's going to bang on it when I touch the puck. Not when I score. When I touch it.

options.text: Want me to stand next to your dad and keep him calm?

say: {owner}! I've got a new fact. It's a good one.
Hey {owner}. Did you see my crossover? You saw it. Right?
What? I'm busy. Okay, not busy.
I'm waiting for Tommy. He owes me a pin. Kind of.

options.text: What do you think of the rink?

fact.say: Okay. Ronnie Haverstock is carrying milk crates in the 1979 Lumber Kings photo, before he was famous. You can see him in the doorway. Your turn.

options.text: Earl's tally wall has over nine thousand floods on it.

fact_earl.say: NINE THOUSAND? Whoa. Okay. That's worth a card. Here. It's a double. Ronnie Haverstock, rookie year.

options.text: Thanks, Owen. I'll keep it safe.
Keep your card. The fact was free.

hockey.say: Good. I play U11 wing. I'm the second-fastest. Little Sauce is faster but he's twelve so it doesn't count. Tommy says I'm worth two Kessler pins.

options.text: Two pins is a good rate.

mason.say: He's quiet. Like, really quiet. But he's really funny if his dad isn't there. He drew Doris with muscles. Best drawing ever.

dad.say: He learned to stop last February. Now he stops everywhere. He stopped in the grocery store. In shoes. And he still can't go backwards. I can.

options.text: You must be a bit proud of him, though.
Don't rub it in too much.

dad_proud.say: ...Maybe. A little. Don't tell him. He'll stop in front of me about it.

rink.say: The hot chocolate sign says HOT CHOC LATE. It's been like that forever. Don't fix it. It's funny.

options.text: The ice is better now, right?
We put real hooks in the dressing rooms.

rink_ice.say: Way better. I did a hockey stop and a big spray came up. Like on TV. Dad tried. He fell.
